title: Language barrier played role in fatal police shooting during standoff: jury
article: FORT ST. JOHN, B.C. - An inquest jury says a language barrier and the lack of an RCMP armoured vehicle in northern B.C. played roles in the fatal police shooting of a man near Fort St. John two years ago.

The jury ruled the death of Valeri George a homicide, caused by gunshot wounds to the chest fired by members of an RCMP emergency response team during an armed standoff outside George's home in September of 2009.
The inquest heard that police fired 47 shots as George, who was carrying a rifle, approached them. Four of the shots struck George and two of those were fatal.
George spoke German, but no officer on the scene did, and the jury recommended the RCMP create a database of officers who speak languages other than English.
The jury also recommended having an armoured vehicle stationed with the North District RCMP after officers told the inquest such a vehicle would have allowed them to get closer to George's home.
George's son-in-law, Jacob Rempel Jr., says not enough was done to try to communicate with the victim, saying George would have responded better to a family member or friend.
"I think, personally, it would really help to get a close family friend or family member in there to try and talk to him, he said.
However, lead investigator Sgt. Dave Chauhan testified it would have been too dangerous to send anyone on to the property.
Several witnesses testified that months before his death, George, who had a wife and 11 children, appeared to be depressed and possibly suffering from a mental illness.
Cpl. Dan Moskaluk, Senior Media Relations Officer for the RCMP in northern B.C. says analysts will study the findings of the inquest jury.
"Certainly we are committed to always reviewing our current policies and practices to always ensure the utmost and best delivery of our police services in our communities," he said.
